DUPLICATES IN PARCC DATA
 AN OVERVIEW

 Damian W Betebenner
National Center for the Improvement of Educational Assessment
 Dover, New Hampshire March15th, 2017

BACKGROUND
• Duplicate cases are defined as cases in the data set the are redundant on
 CONTENT_AREA, YEAR, and ID

• That is, duplicate cases represent situations where more than one test
 record exists in a given CONTENT_AREA and YEAR for a student.

• There are both legitimate and illegitimate reasons for duplicates of this sort.

• Currently we accommodate the duplicates (without getting into the issue
 of whether they are legitimate or illegitimate).

• The problems with duplicates from a growth perspective is that we have to
 accommodate all permutations of current score/prior score duplicates
 leading to potentially a large number of SGPs.

ANALYSIS
• Across all windows of data received thus far, there are 1,398 records
 that would be considered duplicates.

• These records occur in all content areas and years as follows:

 Algebra I Algebra II Geometry Mathematics ELA

 2014-2015.2 2 4 0 32 126

 2015-2016.1 0 0 0 0 46

 2015-2016.2 10 18 4 92 812

 2016-2017.1 0 0 0 0 214

ANALYSIS
• Students with duplicates in one year often have duplicates in other
 years.

• For example, of the 214 ELA duplicates in 2016-2017.1, 106 duplicates
 in 2015-2016.2 had IDs in that set. Not all of those duplicates fit into
 analyzable grade sequences, but some did.

• As we being preparations for the Spring 2016-2017 analyses, we think
 it is necessary to understand:

 • Why these duplicates exist?

 • What states would like done with these duplicates in terms of
 growth analyses.
